title: Themes and current ideas
html:
One home for the theme map and the desk’s current ideas, so every report reads the same thing. Before Nov 9, 2026 these were typed into each report's instructions and could not be updated.

How the reports use this doc

  • Every report (pre-market, nightly) reads this doc and uses it for the themes section, for choosing top names, and for the watchlist rules in watchlist.md.
  • The nightly report updates it:
    • Theme map: each night, change a theme's one-line evidence when the day gave real new evidence (earnings, news, money flow, a leader breaking a level). Add or retire a theme only in the Friday or Sunday report, and say so in that report.
    • Current ideas: change them only when the desk says so, or when a play closes or is cancelled on the scorecard. Never invent a new idea for him here; new candidates go in the report as plays to study.
    • After any change, write the full doc back and update the updated: date and the log.
  • The pre-market briefing only reads it.

the desk’s current ideas (he set these on Nov 7, 2026)

  • Long: DAL (main long focus). PLTR (new focus; uptrend with RSI under 40, on the 50% Fib of the Jun–Oct run plus the 200-day near $153–160).
  • Long, conditional: RCL, only when its options are liquid enough.
  • Downside: BA. DELL (watching $295, then $250 and $200). SMH (watching $427, then below $400). NOW and other weak AI names.
  • Not a focus: HLT. Its options trade too thinly (Nov 6: the Dec $390 call traded 4 contracts). It stays on the watchlist only.
  • More aggressive (the desk, Nov 15): "I want you to be more aggressive in our plays. Like why aren't we already in KO options?" The reports now also take trend-continuation plays in strong uptrends, not only pullbacks to a floor.

His tested edge

  • "Uptrend (price and 50-day above the 200-day) + RSI(14) under 40" has a modest upside edge.
  • "Downtrend + RSI over 60" put setups have worked only on TSLA.
  • Fib levels are the map for entries, stops and targets, not an edge alone.
  • DELL and PLTR are momentum names; dip-buying has been weak on DELL.
  • Not yet tested: trend continuation (strong uptrend, buy the breakout or a shallow dip to the 20-day). Added Nov 15 at the desk’s request; the scorecard tracks it as its own setup type. First closed results: KO $100 C −$128 (Nov 19), AAPL $360 C −$230 (Nov 20); 0-2.
  • Level failure put (Nov 16): 2-0 so far (NVDA $140 P +$1,135, V $405 P +$490); early read.
